---
title: "Why event-driven analytics?"
---

## The limits of snapshot-based analytics

Traditional analytics relies on periodic snapshots — daily reports, weekly
aggregations, monthly summaries. This approach loses the sequence of events
and makes it impossible to answer questions like "what happened between
Tuesday and Thursday that caused the spike?"

## Event-driven advantages

Event-driven analytics preserves the full timeline. With event data you can:

- **Track user journeys** step by step through a funnel
- **Detect anomalies** in real time as they happen
- **Replay history** to understand what led to an outcome
- **Build flexible aggregations** at any time granularity

## When to use event-driven analytics

Event-driven approaches work best when timing and sequence matter — user
behavior analysis, operational monitoring, IoT sensor data, and financial
transaction tracking.

For static, slowly-changing data (annual reports, census data), traditional
snapshot approaches are simpler and sufficient.
